articles.title: SpaceX rocket stage crashes into moon, scientists confirm
articles.titleCn: SpaceX火箭级撞上月球，科学家证实
articles.summary: A SpaceX rocket stage floating in space since last year smashed into the moon at high speed early Wednesday morning, joining the ranks of meteoroids, wayward spacecraft ​and other pieces of space junk that have bombarded the lunar surface for ages, astronomers confirmed.
articles.summaryCn: SpaceX的猎鹰9号火箭上级在2026年8月5日意外撞击月球，引发对太空垃圾和未来月球任务安全的关注。

paragraphs.en: The moon during the morning hours as German astronomers observe the moon surface from their platform of the Observatory Kassel during an international observation campaign following the predicted impact of a SpaceX Falcon 9 upper stage near the lunar Einstein crater, August 5, 2026. A SpaceX rocket stage floating in space since last year {{0}} into the moon at high speed early Wednesday morning, joining the ranks of meteoroids, wayward spacecraft and other pieces of space junk that have {{1}} the lunar surface for ages, astronomers confirmed. The school-bus-size object is the second stage of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket that launched a lunar lander from Firefly Aerospace toward the moon in January 2025. While the rocket's booster returned to Earth, the upper stage remained in space after completing its primary mission. The unintentional collision occurred at around 2:35 a.m.
paragraphs.cn: 2026年8月5日早晨，德国天文学家在卡塞尔天文台平台上观测月球表面，这是针对SpaceX猎鹰9号火箭上级预计撞击月球爱因斯坦陨石坑附近后进行的国际观测活动。天文学家证实，一枚自去年起漂浮在太空中的SpaceX火箭级于周三凌晨高速撞上月球，加入了长期以来轰击月球表面的流星体、偏离轨道的航天器和其他太空垃圾的行列。这个校车大小的物体是SpaceX猎鹰9号火箭的第二级，该火箭于2025年1月将萤火虫航空航天公司的月球着陆器送往月球。虽然火箭的助推器返回了地球，但上级在完成其主要任务后仍留在太空中。这次意外碰撞发生在凌晨2点35分左右。

paragraphs.en: ET (0635 GMT), when the 4,000-kilogram rocket stage slammed into the moon at a speed of about 8,690 kilometers per hour. The impact had been predicted months in advance by astronomers tracking the object's {{2}}. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket lifts off from pad 39A with a payload of a pair of lunar landers at the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida, the US, January 15, 2025. The crash {{3}} no threat to Earth, and no spacecraft orbiting the moon were positioned to capture close-up images of the impact. But the European Southern Observatory's (ESO) Very Large Telescope in Chile detected {{4}} of light associated with the impact.
paragraphs.cn: 美国东部时间（格林尼治标准时间0635）凌晨2点35分左右，这个4000公斤重的火箭级以约8690公里/小时的速度撞击月球。这次撞击在数月前就被追踪该物体轨迹的天文学家预测到了。2025年1月15日，一枚SpaceX猎鹰9号火箭携带一对月球着陆器从美国佛罗里达州卡纳维拉尔角肯尼迪航天中心的39A发射台升空。这次撞击对地球没有威胁，而且月球轨道上也没有航天器能够拍摄到撞击的近距离图像。但智利的欧洲南方天文台（ESO）甚大望远镜探测到了与撞击相关的闪光。

paragraphs.en: "We can confirm that the telescope detected {{5}} lines of sodium and lithium gas in the impact {{6}} lasting for 5-10 minutes after impact," an ESO spokesperson told Reuters. NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter probe and South Korea's Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter were also expected to take images of the impact site, though it could take days to receive that information. The event comes as SpaceX continues to expand its space operations and commercial activities. In its first quarterly report since going public in June, the company reported strong {{7}} growth, with revenue reaching $7.8 billion, up more than 90% from a year earlier. Starlink revenue, which accounted for over half of total revenue, rose 66%, and revenue from SpaceX's AI business – which Musk has pitched as the company's future growth driver – {{8}} about 250%.
paragraphs.cn: “我们可以确认，望远镜在撞击后5到10分钟内探测到了撞击羽流中的钠和锂气体光谱线，”ESO发言人告诉路透社。美国宇航局的月球勘测轨道飞行器探测器和韩国的探路者月球轨道器预计也将拍摄撞击地点的图像，尽管可能需要几天时间才能收到这些信息。这一事件发生之际，SpaceX正继续扩大其太空运营和商业活动。在6月上市以来的首份季度报告中，该公司报告了强劲的收入增长，收入达到78亿美元，同比增长超过90%。占其总收入一半以上的星链收入增长了66%，而SpaceX的人工智能业务（马斯克将其定位为公司未来的增长驱动力）的收入激增了约250%。

paragraphs.en:
However, the stock fell by as much as 8% in after-hours trading following the release, as investors reacted to a sharp increase in capital {{9}}, driven largely by AI infrastructure investments. Space junk raising concern
Space {{14}} has become a growing concern as more satellites and spacecraft enter orbit. Experts have warned that {{10}} too much space junk around Earth could lead to a dangerous {{11}} reaction of collisions known as the "Kessler syndrome."
Generally on such missions, SpaceX performs a {{12}} to make sure the second stage "is safe per the appropriate rules and regulations," said Julianna Scheiman, director of NASA Science and Dragon Programs at SpaceX, at a Monday news conference. "We did that," she continued, but "what has happened is essentially a {{13}} of solar activity and gravity forces have put it on a path towards the moon."
The rocket stage was just one of tens of thousands of pieces of human-made debris currently orbiting Earth. While the moon is constantly bombarded by natural objects such as meteoroids, impacts from artificial spacecraft remain relatively uncommon.
paragraphs.cn: 然而，财报发布后，该股在盘后交易中下跌了多达8%，因为投资者对资本支出的大幅增加做出了反应，这主要是由人工智能基础设施投资推动的。太空垃圾引发担忧。随着越来越多的卫星和航天器进入轨道，太空碎片已成为一个日益令人担忧的问题。专家警告说，地球周围积累过多的太空垃圾可能导致危险的连锁碰撞反应，即所谓的“凯斯勒综合征”。SpaceX负责NASA科学和龙飞船项目的总监朱莉安娜·谢曼在周一的新闻发布会上表示，通常在此类任务中，SpaceX会进行机动，以确保第二级“符合相关规则和法规的安全要求”。“我们做到了，”她继续说，但“发生的事情基本上是太阳活动和引力作用的结合，使其走上了通往月球的路径。”这个火箭级只是目前绕地球运行的数万块人造碎片之一。虽然月球不断受到流星体等自然物体的轰击，但人造航天器的撞击仍然相对罕见。

paragraphs.en: NASA and SpaceX are discussing ways to prevent future lunar impacts, Scheiman said. Under NASA's multibillion-dollar Artemis program, the US space agency plans to build a lunar base and send routine astronaut missions to the lunar surface later this decade. Protecting future spacecraft, equipment and lunar habitats from {{15}} pieces of space junk will become a growing {{16}}. "It's one of the things that we're working in partnership with NASA and the other appropriate agencies is what is the best future {{17}} path for high-energy missions that are in the sun-Earth-moon system," said Scheiman. Despite concerns over space debris, scientists also see research value in the collision.
paragraphs.cn: 谢曼说，NASA和SpaceX正在讨论防止未来月球撞击的方法。根据NASA耗资数十亿美元的阿尔忒弥斯计划，美国航天局计划在本十年晚些时候建立一个月球基地，并定期向月球表面派遣宇航员任务。保护未来的航天器、设备和月球栖息地免受误入歧途的太空垃圾的侵害将成为一个日益重要的优先事项。“这是我们与NASA和其他相关机构合作解决的问题之一，即对于太阳-地球-月球系统中的高能任务，什么是最好的未来处置路径，”谢曼说。尽管对太空碎片感到担忧，但科学家们也看到了这次碰撞的研究价值。

paragraphs.en: NASA intentionally crashed stages from its Saturn V moon rocket into the moon in the 1970s to study the impacts' {{18}} effects. In 2009, the agency intentionally crashed a rocket stage into the moon as part of the LCROSS mission to study the plume of lunar material {{19}} up by the impact, leading to a key discovery that lunar dirt contains traces of water ice. This time, "NASA scientists are planning to collect lunar data from the event and {{20}} techniques for tracking objects in space," the US agency said.
paragraphs.cn: 20世纪70年代，NASA故意将其土星五号月球火箭的各级撞向月球，以研究撞击的地震效应。2009年，该机构作为LCROSS任务的一部分，故意将一枚火箭级撞向月球，以研究撞击掀起的月球物质羽流，从而得出了一项关键发现：月球土壤中含有水冰的痕迹。这一次，“NASA科学家计划从这一事件中收集月球数据，并完善跟踪太空物体的技术，”美国航天局表示。

articles.fullText:
The moon during the morning hours as German astronomers observe the moon surface from their platform of the Observatory Kassel during an international observation campaign following the predicted impact of a SpaceX Falcon 9 upper stage near the lunar Einstein crater, August 5, 2026. 
A SpaceX rocket stage floating in space since last year smashed into the moon at high speed early Wednesday morning, joining the ranks of meteoroids, wayward spacecraft and other pieces of space junk that have bombarded the lunar surface for ages, astronomers confirmed.
The school-bus-size object is the second stage of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket that launched a lunar lander from Firefly Aerospace toward the moon in January 2025. While the rocket's booster returned to Earth, the upper stage remained in space after completing its primary mission.
The unintentional collision occurred at around 2:35 a.m. ET (0635 GMT), when the 4,000-kilogram rocket stage slammed into the moon at a speed of about 8,690 kilometers per hour. The impact had been predicted months in advance by astronomers tracking the object's trajectory.
A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket lifts off from pad 39A with a payload of a pair of lunar landers at the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida, the US, January 15, 2025. 
The crash posed no threat to Earth, and no spacecraft orbiting the moon were positioned to capture close-up images of the impact.
But the European Southern Observatory's (ESO) Very Large Telescope in Chile detected glimmers of light associated with the impact. "We can confirm that the telescope detected spectral lines of sodium and lithium gas in the impact plume lasting for 5-10 minutes after impact," an ESO spokesperson told Reuters.
NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter probe and South Korea's Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter were also expected to take images of the impact site, though it could take days to receive that information.
The event comes as SpaceX continues to expand its space operations and commercial activities. In its first quarterly report since going public in June, the company reported strong revenue growth, with revenue reaching $7.8 billion, up more than 90% from a year earlier. Starlink revenue, which accounted for over half of total revenue, rose 66%, and revenue from SpaceX's AI business – which Musk has pitched as the company's future growth driver – surged about 250%. However, the stock fell by as much as 8% in after-hours trading following the release, as investors reacted to a sharp increase in capital expenditures, driven largely by AI infrastructure investments.
Space junk raising concern
Space debris has become a growing concern as more satellites and spacecraft enter orbit.
Experts have warned that amassing too much space junk around Earth could lead to a dangerous chain reaction of collisions known as the "Kessler syndrome."
Generally on such missions, SpaceX performs a maneuver to make sure the second stage "is safe per the appropriate rules and regulations," said Julianna Scheiman, director of NASA Science and Dragon Programs at SpaceX, at a Monday news conference.
"We did that," she continued, but "what has happened is essentially a mixture of solar activity and gravity forces have put it on a path towards the moon."
The rocket stage was just one of tens of thousands of pieces of human-made debris currently orbiting Earth. While the moon is constantly bombarded by natural objects such as meteoroids, impacts from artificial spacecraft remain relatively uncommon.
NASA and SpaceX are discussing ways to prevent future lunar impacts, Scheiman said. Under NASA's multibillion-dollar Artemis program, the US space agency plans to build a lunar base and send routine astronaut missions to the lunar surface later this decade. Protecting future spacecraft, equipment and lunar habitats from errant pieces of space junk will become a growing priority.
"It's one of the things that we're working in partnership with NASA and the other appropriate agencies is what is the best future disposal path for high-energy missions that are in the sun-Earth-moon system," said Scheiman.
Despite concerns over space debris, scientists also see research value in the collision.
NASA intentionally crashed stages from its Saturn V moon rocket into the moon in the 1970s to study the impacts' seismic effects. In 2009, the agency intentionally crashed a rocket stage into the moon as part of the LCROSS mission to study the plume of lunar material kicked up by the impact, leading to a key discovery that lunar dirt contains traces of water ice.
This time, "NASA scientists are planning to collect lunar data from the event and refine techniques for tracking objects in space," the US agency said.

articles.title: Scientists reveal how aging weakens the brain's protective barrier
articles.titleCn: 科学家揭示衰老如何削弱大脑的保护屏障
articles.summary: Scientists reveal how aging weakens the brain's protective barrier
articles.summaryCn: 研究发现衰老通过TGF-β1信号增加脑内皮细胞转运，导致血脑屏障渗漏，进而影响认知功能。

paragraphs.en:
As people age, many experience memory decline and slower {{0}} processing, along with a higher risk of {{1}} disease and cognitive {{2}}. One important question in aging research is how changes in the brain's blood vessels contribute to cognitive decline. Scientists from the Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology (SIAT) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have identified a {{3}} by which aging weakens the blood-brain barrier, the brain's protective {{4}} with the bloodstream. The study was published in Neuron under the title "TGF-β1-induced endothelial {{5}} drives blood-brain barrier leakage during aging."
The study shows how aging {{6}} transport in brain blood vessel cells, leading to blood-brain barrier leakage. /SIAT
The blood-brain barrier, or BBB, acts as a {{7}} security system.
paragraphs.cn: 随着人们年龄增长，许多人会经历记忆力下降和认知处理速度变慢，同时患脑血管疾病和认知障碍的风险也会增加。衰老研究中的一个重要问题是大脑血管的变化如何导致认知衰退。中国科学院深圳先进技术研究院（SIAT）的科学家们识别出衰老削弱血脑屏障（大脑与血液之间的保护性界面）的一种机制。该研究发表在《神经元》杂志上，标题为“TGF-β1诱导的内皮细胞转胞吞作用驱动衰老过程中的血脑屏障渗漏”。研究显示衰老如何扰乱脑血管细胞中的运输，导致血脑屏障渗漏。/SIAT 血脑屏障（BBB）像一个选择性安全系统。

paragraphs.en: It allows {{8}} nutrients to reach the brain while preventing potentially {{9}} substances in the blood from entering brain tissue. Damage to this barrier has been linked to cognitive aging, cerebral small vessel disease and several {{10}} disorders. Scientists have traditionally {{11}} BBB leakage mainly to damage to the tight seals between cells lining brain blood vessels. However, the new study found that another process occurs earlier during aging. By examining mice at different ages, the researchers found that BBB leakage was already {{12}} in middle-aged mice and worsened in older animals.
paragraphs.cn: 它允许必需营养物质到达大脑，同时防止血液中潜在有害物质进入脑组织。这种屏障的损伤与认知衰老、脑小血管疾病和多种神经退行性疾病有关。科学家传统上将血脑屏障渗漏主要归因于脑内血管内壁细胞之间紧密连接的损伤。然而，新研究发现另一个过程在衰老过程中更早发生。通过检查不同年龄的小鼠，研究人员发现血脑屏障渗漏在中年小鼠中已可检测到，并在老年动物中恶化。

paragraphs.en: The change appeared early in the {{13}}, a brain region important for learning and memory. At this stage, the seals between blood vessel cells remained largely {{14}}. Instead, the cells' internal transport system became {{15}} active, allowing blood-borne substances to pass through the cells and enter brain tissue. "Rather than first leaking through gaps between cells, the aging blood-brain barrier appears to lose control over transport pathways inside the cells," the researchers said. The team identified a protein called Mfsd2a as an important part of this protective system.
paragraphs.cn: 这种变化早期出现在海马体，这是一个对学习和记忆重要的大脑区域。在这个阶段，血管细胞之间的连接基本保持完整。相反，细胞内部的运输系统变得异常活跃，允许血液中的物质穿过细胞进入脑组织。研究人员说：“衰老的血脑屏障似乎不是首先通过细胞间隙渗漏，而是失去了对细胞内运输途径的控制。”团队识别出一种名为Mfsd2a的蛋白质，作为这一保护系统的重要组成部分。

paragraphs.en: Mfsd2a normally limits unnecessary transport across brain blood vessels. Its levels declined with age, while Caveolin-1, a protein involved in the formation of transport vesicles, increased. When the researchers {{16}} endothelial Mfsd2a expression or {{17}} down Caveolin-1 in aged mice, abnormal vesicle transport and BBB leakage were significantly reduced. The researchers then investigated why Mfsd2a declines during aging. They found that levels of TGF-β1, a signaling molecule involved in inflammation, tissue repair and aging, increased in both the brain and the bloodstream as mice aged.

articles.fullText:
As people age, many experience memory decline and slower cognitive processing, along with a higher risk of cerebrovascular disease and cognitive impairment. One important question in aging research is how changes in the brain's blood vessels contribute to cognitive decline.
Scientists from the Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology (SIAT) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have identified a mechanism by which aging weakens the blood-brain barrier, the brain's protective interface with the bloodstream.
The study was published in Neuron under the title "TGF-β1-induced endothelial transcytosis drives blood-brain barrier leakage during aging."
The study shows how aging disrupts transport in brain blood vessel cells, leading to blood-brain barrier leakage. /SIAT
The blood-brain barrier, or BBB, acts as a selective security system. It allows essential nutrients to reach the brain while preventing potentially harmful substances in the blood from entering brain tissue. Damage to this barrier has been linked to cognitive aging, cerebral small vessel disease and several neurodegenerative disorders.
Scientists have traditionally attributed BBB leakage mainly to damage to the tight seals between cells lining brain blood vessels. However, the new study found that another process occurs earlier during aging.
By examining mice at different ages, the researchers found that BBB leakage was already detectable in middle-aged mice and worsened in older animals. The change appeared early in the hippocampus, a brain region important for learning and memory.
At this stage, the seals between blood vessel cells remained largely intact. Instead, the cells' internal transport system became abnormally active, allowing blood-borne substances to pass through the cells and enter brain tissue.
"Rather than first leaking through gaps between cells, the aging blood-brain barrier appears to lose control over transport pathways inside the cells," the researchers said.
The team identified a protein called Mfsd2a as an important part of this protective system. Mfsd2a normally limits unnecessary transport across brain blood vessels. Its levels declined with age, while Caveolin-1, a protein involved in the formation of transport vesicles, increased.
When the researchers restored endothelial Mfsd2a expression or knocked down Caveolin-1 in aged mice, abnormal vesicle transport and BBB leakage were significantly reduced.
The researchers then investigated why Mfsd2a declines during aging. They found that levels of TGF-β1, a signaling molecule involved in inflammation, tissue repair and aging, increased in both the brain and the bloodstream as mice aged.
Excessive TGF-β1 reduced Mfsd2a expression in the cells lining brain blood vessels, causing their transport activity to increase. Raising TGF-β1 levels in young mice caused them to develop several features normally seen in the aged BBB, including increased leakage.
By contrast, blocking TGF-β signaling in aged mice reduced BBB leakage and improved their performance in memory-related behavioral tests.
The findings suggest that age-related BBB damage is not simply the result of passive wear and tear. Instead, it involves biological signals that alter how brain blood vessel cells transport substances.
The study may help explain how vascular changes contribute to cognitive aging. It also points to potential approaches for protecting the aging brain, including maintaining Mfsd2a function or preventing excessive activation of TGF-β signaling. Further research will be needed to determine whether these strategies can be safely translated into treatments for humans.
articles.fullTextCn:
随着人们年龄增长，许多人会经历记忆力下降和认知处理速度变慢，同时患脑血管疾病和认知障碍的风险也会增加。衰老研究中的一个重要问题是大脑血管的变化如何导致认知衰退。中国科学院深圳先进技术研究院（SIAT）的科学家们识别出衰老削弱血脑屏障（大脑与血液之间的保护性界面）的一种机制。该研究发表在《神经元》杂志上，标题为“TGF-β1诱导的内皮细胞转胞吞作用驱动衰老过程中的血脑屏障渗漏”。研究显示衰老如何扰乱脑血管细胞中的运输，导致血脑屏障渗漏。/SIAT 血脑屏障（BBB）像一个选择性安全系统。

它允许必需营养物质到达大脑，同时防止血液中潜在有害物质进入脑组织。这种屏障的损伤与认知衰老、脑小血管疾病和多种神经退行性疾病有关。科学家传统上将血脑屏障渗漏主要归因于脑内血管内壁细胞之间紧密连接的损伤。然而，新研究发现另一个过程在衰老过程中更早发生。通过检查不同年龄的小鼠，研究人员发现血脑屏障渗漏在中年小鼠中已可检测到，并在老年动物中恶化。

这种变化早期出现在海马体，这是一个对学习和记忆重要的大脑区域。在这个阶段，血管细胞之间的连接基本保持完整。相反，细胞内部的运输系统变得异常活跃，允许血液中的物质穿过细胞进入脑组织。研究人员说：“衰老的血脑屏障似乎不是首先通过细胞间隙渗漏，而是失去了对细胞内运输途径的控制。”团队识别出一种名为Mfsd2a的蛋白质，作为这一保护系统的重要组成部分。

Mfsd2a通常限制大脑血管中不必要的运输。其水平随年龄增长而下降，而参与运输囊泡形成的蛋白质Caveolin-1则增加。当研究人员在老年小鼠中恢复内皮Mfsd2a表达或敲低Caveolin-1时，异常囊泡运输和血脑屏障渗漏显著减少。研究人员随后调查了为什么Mfsd2a在衰老过程中下降。他们发现，随着小鼠年龄增长，大脑和血液中TGF-β1（一种参与炎症、组织修复和衰老的信号分子）的水平增加。

过量的TGF-β1降低了脑内血管内壁细胞中Mfsd2a的表达，导致其运输活性增加。在年轻小鼠中提高TGF-β1水平，使它们出现通常见于衰老血脑屏障的多种特征，包括渗漏增加。相比之下，在老年小鼠中阻断TGF-β信号减少了血脑屏障渗漏，并改善了它们在记忆相关行为测试中的表现。这些发现表明，与年龄相关的血脑屏障损伤不仅仅是被动磨损的结果。相反，它涉及改变脑血管细胞运输物质的生物信号。

这项研究可能有助于解释血管变化如何导致认知衰老。它还指出了保护衰老大脑的潜在方法，包括维持Mfsd2a功能或防止TGF-β信号过度激活。需要进一步研究来确定这些策略是否能安全地转化为人类治疗方法。

articles.fullText:
The 25th China Internet Conference opens at the China National Convention Center in Beijing, capital of China, July 8, 2026. 
Artificial intelligence is moving rapidly from experimental technology to real-world applications, as industry leaders showcased new AI-powered solutions for cities, businesses and consumers at the 25th China Internet Conference in Beijing.
Held from July 8 to 10, the conference highlighted how AI agents, large language models and digital twin technologies are being integrated into sectors ranging from urban governance and industrial manufacturing to retail and public services.
Speaking via video at the opening ceremony, Wu Hequan, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering, said AI-native technologies are reshaping the internet itself.
While large language models excel at general reasoning, AI agents are designed to execute specific tasks and future digital ecosystems will increasingly rely on collaboration among multiple intelligent agents rather than isolated AI systems.
Participants of the 25th China Internet Conference try on VR products at the China National Convention Center in Beijing, capital of China, July 8, 2026. 
According to Wu, AI-generated traffic is expected to account for around 60% of global internet traffic by 2030, with AI agent services becoming the dominant source of token-based interactions. The shift, he said, will require internet infrastructure to evolve toward higher bandwidth, lower latency and stronger computing capabilities.
The conference also demonstrated how AI is being deployed in practical scenarios. Digital assistants are supporting office collaboration and customer services, while AI-powered inspection systems are improving industrial operations. Digital twin technologies are enabling more efficient traffic management, energy optimization and building maintenance, providing city managers with real-time visualization and decision-making tools.
Industry representatives also emphasized that AI innovation is creating measurable economic value.
Participants of the 25th China Internet Conference interact with humanoid robots at the China National Convention Center in Beijing, capital of China, July 8, 2026. 
At the conference, Kuaishou said its AI-powered video generation model and digital human live-streaming platform have helped small and medium-sized businesses increase daily gross merchandise value while significantly reducing marketing costs. Alibaba's Taobao Instant Commerce platform reported that AI agents are increasingly handling complex shopping requests, moving beyond traditional keyword-based searches to task-oriented consumer services.
Beyond applications, participants identified trustworthy AI and green computing as key priorities for the industry's next stage of development. The launch of the FlagOS Initiative, an open AI software platform designed to improve compatibility across different computing chips, reflects broader efforts to build more efficient and sustainable AI infrastructure.
As AI technologies continue to mature, industry experts believe the focus is shifting from developing models to deploying them at scale. The conference highlighted China's efforts to accelerate AI adoption across the real economy, with intelligent applications increasingly becoming part of everyday life while supporting digital transformation and high-quality economic development.

articles.title: ICC oversight body urges Chad and Venezuela to reverse withdrawal
articles.titleCn: 国际刑事法院监督机构敦促乍得和委内瑞拉撤回退出决定
articles.summary: The body that oversees the International Criminal Court has urged Chad and Venezuela to reconsider their decisions to withdraw from the court, warning that their departures could undermine global efforts to fight impunity.
articles.summaryCn: 国际刑事法院监督机构呼吁乍得和委内瑞拉重新考虑退出决定，警告此举可能削弱全球打击有罪不罚的努力。

paragraphs.en: The body that oversees the International Criminal Court (ICC) has {{1}} Chad and Venezuela to reconsider their decisions to withdraw from the court, warning that their departures could {{3}} global efforts to fight {{4}}. In a statement issued on Friday from The Hague, the Assembly of States Parties said it viewed the {{2}} announcements "with {{5}}" and called on both countries to remain members of the court. The assembly encouraged them to address any concerns through {{6}} within the ICC system rather than leaving the institution. The appeal comes as the court faces its most {{7}} wave of withdrawal announcements since it was {{8}} in 2002. Five countries have said they intend to leave the ICC since last year, amid {{9}} international pressure on the tribunal.
paragraphs.cn: 负责监督国际刑事法院的机构已敦促乍得和委内瑞拉重新考虑退出法院的决定，警告称它们的退出可能削弱全球打击有罪不罚的努力。缔约国大会周五在海牙发表声明，表示对退出公告“表示关切”，并呼吁两国继续留在法院。大会鼓励它们通过国际刑事法院体系内的对话解决任何关切，而不是离开该机构。这一呼吁发出之际，法院正面临自2002年成立以来最大规模的退出公告浪潮。自去年以来，已有五个国家表示打算退出国际刑事法院，而该法庭正面临新的国际压力。

paragraphs.en: Chad announced its withdrawal on July 27, arguing that the court's record had been {{10}} and {{11}} focused on Africa. Officials noted that six of the seven suspects currently in ICC {{12}} are linked to African cases. Venezuela announced its withdrawal three days earlier. Foreign Minister Felix Plasencia told the United Nations that the decision, ordered by Interim President Delcy Rodríguez, was "firm and {{13}}" and accused the court of {{14}} bias against Africa and Latin America. Under the Rome Statute, the ICC's founding treaty, a withdrawal takes effect one year after notification.
paragraphs.cn: 乍得于7月27日宣布退出，认为法院的记录不均衡，且过分聚焦于非洲。官员指出，目前被国际刑事法院羁押的七名嫌疑人中有六名与非洲案件有关。委内瑞拉在三天前宣布退出。外交部长费利克斯·普拉森西亚告诉联合国，由临时总统德尔西·罗德里格斯下令的这一决定是“坚定且不可撤销的”，并指责法院对非洲和拉丁美洲存在地理偏见。根据《罗马规约》（国际刑事法院的创始条约），退出在通知后一年生效。

articles.fullText:
The body that oversees the International Criminal Court (ICC) has urged Chad and Venezuela to reconsider their decisions to withdraw from the court, warning that their departures could undermine global efforts to fight impunity.
In a statement issued on Friday from The Hague, the Assembly of States Parties said it viewed the withdrawal announcements "with concern" and called on both countries to remain members of the court. The assembly encouraged them to address any concerns through dialogue within the ICC system rather than leaving the institution.
The appeal comes as the court faces its most significant wave of withdrawal announcements since it was established in 2002. Five countries have said they intend to leave the ICC since last year, amid renewed international pressure on the tribunal.
Chad announced its withdrawal on July 27, arguing that the court's record had been uneven and disproportionately focused on Africa. Officials noted that six of the seven suspects currently in ICC custody are linked to African cases.
Venezuela announced its withdrawal three days earlier. Foreign Minister Felix Plasencia told the United Nations that the decision, ordered by Interim President Delcy Rodríguez, was "firm and irrevocable" and accused the court of geographic bias against Africa and Latin America.
Under the Rome Statute, the ICC's founding treaty, a withdrawal takes effect one year after notification.
A departing state remains bound by its obligations during that period, and existing investigations and proceedings can continue.
The ICC's investigation into Venezuela is therefore expected to proceed regardless of the withdrawal announcement.
Chad and Venezuela join Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, which announced plans to leave the court last year.
The ICC has also faced mounting pressure from the administration of US President Donald Trump, which has pledged a broad effort to curb the court's authority.
US officials have criticized the ICC over its arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in connection with alleged war crimes in Gaza, as well as the court's investigation into alleged crimes involving foreign forces, including US personnel, in Afghanistan.

负责监督国际刑事法院的机构已敦促乍得和委内瑞拉重新考虑退出法院的决定，警告称它们的退出可能削弱全球打击有罪不罚的努力。缔约国大会周五在海牙发表声明，表示对退出公告“表示关切”，并呼吁两国继续留在法院。大会鼓励它们通过国际刑事法院体系内的对话解决任何关切，而不是离开该机构。这一呼吁发出之际，法院正面临自2002年成立以来最大规模的退出公告浪潮。自去年以来，已有五个国家表示打算退出国际刑事法院，而该法庭正面临新的国际压力。

乍得于7月27日宣布退出，认为法院的记录不均衡，且过分聚焦于非洲。官员指出，目前被国际刑事法院羁押的七名嫌疑人中有六名与非洲案件有关。委内瑞拉在三天前宣布退出。外交部长费利克斯·普拉森西亚告诉联合国，由临时总统德尔西·罗德里格斯下令的这一决定是“坚定且不可撤销的”，并指责法院对非洲和拉丁美洲存在地理偏见。根据《罗马规约》（国际刑事法院的创始条约），退出在通知后一年生效。

退出国家在该期间内仍受其义务约束，现有调查和诉讼可以继续。因此，预计国际刑事法院对委内瑞拉的调查将不受退出公告的影响。乍得和委内瑞拉加入了去年宣布计划退出法院的布基纳法索、马里和尼日尔的行列。国际刑事法院还面临美国总统唐纳德·特朗普政府的日益增大的压力，该政府承诺采取广泛措施限制法院的权力。美国官员批评国际刑事法院对以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡发出逮捕令，该逮捕令与加沙涉嫌战争罪有关，以及法院对阿富汗涉嫌涉及外国军队（包括美国人员）的罪行的调查。

paragraphs.cn: 土耳其执政联盟周三表示，已向议会提交立法草案，旨在建立实施库尔德工人党（PKK）解除武装的法律框架，这是推进政府终结库尔德工人党叛乱倡议的关键一步。执政党正义与发展党（AKP）及其盟友支持该草案，并获得了亲库尔德的人民平等与民主党（DEM）及其他反对派团体的支持，执政党议员阿卜杜拉·居勒告诉记者。据政府称，拟议立法旨在促进解除武装进程，而非给予全面大赦。该法案将允许未参与杀戮或其他严重暴力犯罪的低级库尔德工人党成员，在特定法律条件下从伊拉克北部和叙利亚的藏身地返回土耳其。根据拟议法律框架，未直接参与武装袭击或爆炸事件的囚犯可能有资格获释或接受监督缓刑，而库尔德工人党创始人阿卜杜拉·奥贾兰、高级领导人和被判加重终身监禁的囚犯则被排除在外。草案必须先经议会委员会批准，然后提交大国民议会表决，预计议员们将在本月晚些时候议会夏季休会前就该法案进行辩论。自1984年以来一直对土耳其国家发动叛乱的库尔德工人党，在奥贾兰呼吁结束武装斗争后，于2025年5月宣布决定解除武装并解散。这场持续数十年的冲突已夺去超过4万人的生命。（封面：2026年3月21日，伊拉克东北部，靠近伊拉克-伊朗-土耳其边境的扎格罗斯山脉坎迪尔山区，库尔德工人党成员跳舞庆祝诺鲁孜新年节日。）

articles.fullText:
Türkiye's ruling alliance said Wednesday it had submitted draft legislation to parliament to establish a legal framework for implementing the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK)'s disarmament, a key step in advancing the government's initiative to end PKK insurgency.
The draft legislation has been endorsed by President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's Justice and Development Party (AKP) and its ally, and has also received backing from the pro-Kurdish DEM Party and other opposition groups, Abdullah Guler, a leading AKP lawmaker, told reporters.
According to the government, the proposed legislation is designed to facilitate the disarmament process rather than grant a general amnesty.
It would allow lower-ranking PKK members who have not been involved in killings or other serious violent crimes to return to Türkiye from hideouts in northern Iraq and Syria under specified legal conditions.
Inmates who were not directly involved in armed attacks or bombings could become eligible for release or supervised probation under the proposed legal framework, while imprisoned PKK founder Abdullah Ocalan, senior PKK leaders and inmates serving aggravated life sentences are excluded.
The draft must first be approved by a parliamentary committee before being put to a vote in the General Assembly, where lawmakers are expected to debate the bill before parliament begins its summer recess later this month.
The PKK, which has waged an insurgency against the Turkish state since 1984, announced in May 2025 its decision to disarm and disband, following a call by Ocalan to end the armed struggle. The decades-long conflict has claimed more than 40,000 lives.
